Willoughby was bred in Canada for genuine cold hardiness and good resistance to American gooseberry mildew, producing medium, deep red berries with a well-balanced sweet-tart flavor good for fresh eating and cooking alike. The productive, reliable bush handles harsh northern winters better than many European-type gooseberries, making it a solid choice for cold-climate home orchards wanting good disease resistance without sacrificing fruit quality. Harvest when berries reach full color and slightly soften, and pick regularly through the ripening window, since gooseberries can be used both underripe and tart for cooking or fully ripe and sweet for fresh eating depending on preference.

Welcome was developed in Canada from American gooseberry (Ribes hirtellum) stock, valued for combining good resistance to American gooseberry mildew — the disease that plagues many older European-type varieties — with reliable production of medium red berries carrying a pleasant, well-balanced sweet-tart flavor. The upright, moderately vigorous bush is easier to manage and harvest than more sprawling heirloom types, and its cold hardiness suits it well to northern home gardens. Harvest when berries reach full color and slightly soften for fresh eating, or pick a bit earlier and firmer for pies, jams, and other cooked preparations where tartness is desired.

directions: Plant dormant bushes in fall or early spring in fertile, well-drained soil, and prune annually to an open center for good air movement. Fredonia is an American-type gooseberry, bred from the same disease-resistant Ribes hirtellum lineage used in many modern hardy gooseberry releases, producing dark red, sweet-tart berries with good flavor and much better tolerance of American gooseberry mildew than older European heirloom varieties. The compact, manageable bush fits well into smaller home gardens, and its reliable, moderate productivity makes it a practical choice for growers who want a straightforward, low-fuss gooseberry without extensive mildew management. Harvest when berries reach full color and slightly soften for fresh eating, or pick a bit earlier for cooking and preserving, since gooseberries hold well on the bush at multiple ripeness stages.

directions: Plant dormant bushes in fall or early spring in fertile, well-drained soil, siting for good air circulation, and prune annually to an open center. Chautauqua is a large-fruited English-type dessert gooseberry, producing pale yellow-green berries considerably larger than most American-type varieties, with a rich, sweet flavor well suited to fresh eating out of hand rather than only cooking, a genuine treat among gooseberries where many varieties lean more tart. Because it descends primarily from European Ribes uva-crispa stock rather than the mildew-resistant American Ribes hirtellum lineage, it is more susceptible to American gooseberry mildew and benefits from a well-ventilated planting site and attentive pruning to reduce disease pressure. Harvest when berries reach full color and soften slightly for the sweetest dessert-quality fruit.

Clark is a Canadian-bred gooseberry hybrid selected for genuinely heavy, reliable production combined with good resistance to American gooseberry mildew, producing medium to large, red-pink berries with a well-balanced sweet-tart flavor good for both fresh eating and cooking. The vigorous, productive bush has made it a favorite among home orchardists in colder regions who want dependable yields without the mildew management headaches that plague more disease-susceptible European heirloom varieties. Harvest when berries reach full color and slightly soften for the sweetest fresh eating, or pick a touch earlier and firmer for pies, jams, and fools where a tarter flavor is preferred.
